result.summary: Read core-directives.md and security-invariants.md (all S1-S14) in full, docs/agents/design/REQ-027.md in full, then the actual diff myself (git diff master...HEAD) rather than trusting BACKEND-DEV's or REVIEWER's characterizations: domain/registration.ts's new selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent block (full diff), handlers/event.ts's new composeCancellationMessage/notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants/makeEventCancelHandler diff (full), index.ts's one-line wiring change, i18n additions (en/ru/types), and apps/bot/src/handlers/event.db.test.ts (full, new file, AC1-AC5 job-level DB tests). S13 STRUCTURAL TRACE (task item 3): read all three new functions line by line. selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent is a plain db.select(...).from(registrations).where(...) with no .update/.insert/.delete call anywhere in the statement chain -- a read only, confirmed by the absence of any db.update/db.delete token in the file's diff hunk for this function. composeCancellationMessage calls only getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent (domain/registration.ts, REQ-026, unchanged by this diff -- confirmed via `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/domain/registration.ts` showing only the new selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent block added, the pre-existing getRegistrationAdmissionAndEvent function is untouched) which is itself a plain SELECT, and returns a ComposedMessage value -- it performs no DB write of any kind. notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants only reads (via the two functions above) and calls sendLedgeredNotification, whose only write is the notification_ledger INSERT (domain/notification.ts, unchanged by this diff -- confirmed `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/domain/notification.ts` is empty, 0 lines). So no function introduced or touched by this diff issues any UPDATE/DELETE against `registrations`, and `cancelEvent` (domain/event.ts, REQ-016) is confirmed BYTE-FOR-BYTE UNTOUCHED: `git diff master...HEAD -- apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts` produces 0 lines of output. Read cancelEvent directly (lines ~660-670) to confirm its transaction still performs exactly the events.status UPDATE and one audit_log INSERT, no registrations table access. AC4's own DB test (event.db.test.ts, 'AC4: registrations rows are untouched') independently confirms every registration row's admission field is unchanged after cancellation + notification, run against real Postgres (see command output below). S13's own migration-signoff trigger does not apply: `git diff --name-only master...HEAD` contains zero files under apps/bot/drizzle/ -- no migration ships with this diff, matching the design doc's 'Schema change: NO' header, confirmed by absence rather than by trusting the design doc's claim. S9 LEDGER-INSERT-THEN-SEND REUSE (task item 4): confirmed notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants calls the EXISTING sendLedgeredNotification (domain/notification.ts, unchanged -- see above) once per candidate in a plain sequential for...of loop, passing kind: 'event_cancelled' (already a pre-existing NotificationKind union member per the design doc's schema-check section, confirmed unmodified) -- this is not a new, parallel send mechanism; it is the same function REQ-025/026 already established, called from a new call site with a new kind value. Read sendLedgeredNotification's body directly: step 4's atomic INSERT against notification_ledger (uniqueIndex on (registrationId, kind), schema.ts unchanged by this diff) is still the sole write and sole idempotency mechanism, unconditionally reached before any composeMessage/send call (step 5). A duplicate INSERT for the same (registrationId, 'event_cancelled') pair still hits the unique index and returns {kind:'skipped-already-sent'} with no send. notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants itself keeps no in-memory state (no local set/counter) -- re-invoking it (whether by a genuine repeat call or a process restart mid-batch) reduces every call to the same duplicate-key no-op, per S9's own explicit warning against in-memory-set idempotency. Verified for real with the AC2 DB test (see below): two full invocations of notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants over the same event -- run 1 sends 2, run 2 sends 0, and exactly 1 ledger row per registration exists after both runs combined. S10 UNCONDITIONAL TRANSACTIONAL CLASSIFICATION (task item 5): read notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants's sendLedgeredNotification call site directly -- classification: 'transactional' is a bare string literal in the object literal passed to sendLedgeredNotification, not a variable, not a ternary, not read from any config/flag. There is exactly one call site (the for...of loop body) and it is unconditional -- no branch anywhere in notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants, composeCancellationMessage, or selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent computes or forwards a classification value; the literal is hardcoded at the one place it's used. Traced sendLedgeredNotification's step 3 (domain/notification.ts, unchanged) -- broadcastOptIn is read ONLY inside `if (input.classification === 'marketing')`, so a 'transactional' call never reads or is gated by broadcastOptIn at all, structurally, not by luck. Verified for real with the AC3 DB test: a registrant seeded with broadcastOptIn: false still receives exactly 1 send and gets exactly 1 ledger row. AUTHORIZATION (task item 6): read makeEventCancelHandler's full body (both the unchanged portion above the diff and the new lines). The existing `requireOrganizerForChapter(db, BigInt(tgId), event.chapterId)` gate (domain/eventAuthorization.ts, confirmed absent from `git diff --name-only master...HEAD` -- this file is untouched by the diff) still runs BEFORE cancelEvent and BEFORE the new notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants call, in the same position it occupied before this requirement (REQ-016). Adding the `sender` parameter only changed the function's own signature (one new parameter threaded through from index.ts's single process-wide notificationSender instance, confirmed by reading index.ts's one-line diff) and added two new lines AFTER the existing authorization/state-machine checks (organizer check, then event.status !== 'published' guard) -- neither check was moved, weakened, or made conditional on the new parameter. Also confirmed the event.status !== 'published' guard is unchanged and, combined with cancelEvent's own status transition (events.status union is 'draft'|'published'|'cancelled' with no path back to 'published' -- confirmed by grepping domain/event.ts for every `.set({ status: ... })` call: only draft->published (publishEvent) and published->cancelled (cancelEvent) exist, no reverse transition anywhere in the file), means a second /event_cancel invocation against the same event is refused by this pre-existing guard before ever reaching cancelEvent or notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants -- see the repeated-trigger finding below. PII/EXPOSURE IN THE NEW MESSAGE (task item 7): read composeCancellationMessage's composed text directly -- three lines: catalog.event.cancelledNotificationHeader (static placeholder copy), eventTitle (the cancelled event's own title, already known to every registrant of that event), catalog.event.deepLinkSeeUpcoming (an already-existing, previously-shipped static string, REQ-017, unchanged). No registrant count, no registrant list, no other registrant's name/phone/email/employer, no capacity or seats-taken figure appears anywhere in the composed text or in any of the three new functions' parameters/return values. selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent's own return type ({registrationId, userId}[]) is consumed only to drive the per-candidate loop -- its length is never read, logged, or surfaced anywhere (no `.length`, no count variable in the diff). Each recipient's message is generated independently per-candidate inside the loop and scoped only to that candidate's own registrationId; nothing about the batch's size or membership crosses into any individual message. S3/S11 hold. BLAST-RADIUS / REPEATED-TRIGGER CHECK (task item 8, specifically requested): traced whether an organizer can cause repeated notification attempts via rapid cancel/re-cancel. The event status-machine is strictly forward-only and has exactly one path to 'cancelled' with no reverse transition (confirmed above by grepping every status-set call in domain/event.ts) -- once cancelEvent commits events.status = 'cancelled', the SAME handler's own `if (event.status !== 'published')` guard (evaluated on a fresh getEventById read at the top of every /event_cancel invocation) refuses any subsequent /event_cancel call against that event with cancelRefusedNotPublished, BEFORE reaching cancelEvent or notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants at all -- so a literal rapid-fire re-run of /event_cancel on the same event id cannot even reach the notification batch a second time; it is refused at the state-machine guard, not merely deduplicated at the ledger. There is no 'uncancel' command anywhere in the codebase (grepped for any `status: 'published'` SET applied to an already-cancelled event -- publishEvent's own guard is presumably scoped to draft-only, and no cancel-reversal handler exists in handlers/event.ts or index.ts's command registrations) so no sequence of organizer actions can move the event back to 'published' and re-open the cancel path. The only way to trigger a second real batch of sends is a genuinely NEW event with an overlapping registrant set, cancelled separately -- that produces legitimate new notifications for a distinct entity (a different eventId, different registrationIds), not a spam amplification of the same cancellation; each such batch is itself bounded by that event's own non-withdrawn registrant count and still deduplicated per (registrationId, kind) if that exact call were somehow re-entered. Separately, even setting the state-machine guard aside, S9's ledger dedup (verified above, AC2) means that even a hypothetical direct call to notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants bypassing the handler (not reachable through any exposed command surface) would still send nothing extra on a second invocation over the same eventId. CONCLUSION: the repeated-trigger scenario is not reachable through the command surface at all (state-machine guard refuses first), and would be a ledger no-op even if it were (defense in depth) -- no spam vector found. COMMANDS RUN BY ME, REAL OUTPUT: `npm run lint` (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors, 2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings (Footer.tsx, Nav.tsx), unrelated to this diff. `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces clean (Next.js + bot tsc). `npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root) -> 24 files / 260 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- ran again scoped to `apps/bot/src/handlers/event.db.test.ts` alone to confirm no 'skipping DB-backed suite' warning appeared (none did, confirming the scratch Postgres at localhost:55432 was reachable and the AC1-AC5 tests actually exercised real DB state, not a silently-skipped no-op run) -> 1 file / 5 tests passed. Read the AC2 and AC3 test bodies directly (not just their names) to confirm they assert real ledger-row counts and real sent-message counts, not just 'no error thrown'. Remaining S1-S14 items, each re-derived against this diff specifically: - S1 (consent precedes storage): N/A -- no User/Profile consent-column writes anywhere in this diff; confirmed by reading every new/changed file for any write to consent_pd_at/broadcast_opt_in/publish_consent -- none exists. - S2: PASS -- see authorization section above; requireOrganizerForChapter unchanged and unconditionally gates before both cancelEvent and the new notify call; the negative case (a non-organizer attempting /event_cancel) is unchanged pre-existing behavior from REQ-016, not touched by this diff. - S3 (member reads only own Profile / no cross-registrant leak): PASS -- see PII/exposure section above; each composed message is scoped to its own recipient only, no count/list/other-registrant data surfaced. - S4 (tokens unguessable): N/A -- no token generation or validation in this diff. - S5/S6/S7 (check-in refusal/audit, checked_in_at gating, capacity+override audit): N/A -- no check-in or capacity code touched; handlers/checkin.ts absent from `git diff --name-only master...HEAD`. - S8 (exactly one AuditLog row per status change): N/A for this diff's own new code (it introduces no new status change -- notification sends are not status changes) -- cancelEvent's existing single audit_log INSERT is unchanged (confirmed byte-for-byte untouched above), still the only audit write in the cancellation flow. - S9: PASS -- see ledger-insert-then-send reuse section above, verified with AC2's real DB test. - S10: PASS -- see unconditional transactional classification section above, verified with AC3's real DB test. - S11 (PII never in plaintext logs): checked all three new functions and the modified handler for any console./log. call -- zero matches (grepped the diff hunks directly); no new logging introduced by this requirement. - S12 (exports role-gated/audited): N/A -- no export functionality in this diff. - S13: PASS -- see S13 structural trace above (registrations never written/deleted by any function in this diff; cancelEvent byte-for-byte untouched; no migration ships with this diff, sign-off trigger not met). - S14 (publication consent default-off): N/A -- no Profile/publish_consent code touched. Scope/hygiene check: `git status --short` clean before and after my review (no scratch files needed -- the producer's own event.db.test.ts already exercised AC1-AC5 against real Postgres, so no separate adversarial test file was necessary for this diff's risk profile). Verdict: PASS. S9, S10, and S13 all hold under independent structural re-derivation (not the producer's self-report), authorization is unweakened, no new PII/group-size leak was introduced, and the rapid cancel/re-cancel spam scenario is not reachable through the command surface (state-machine guard refuses it before the notification batch, with ledger dedup as defense in depth regardless). No blocking defect found across S1-S14. This is the last requirement of Phase 5.

evidence.s13_structural_trace: No function introduced by this diff (selectNonWithdrawnRegistrantsForEvent, composeCancellationMessage, notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants) issues any UPDATE/DELETE against `registrations` -- confirmed by reading each function's full body; cancelEvent (REQ-016) is confirmed byte-for-byte untouched via an empty git diff on domain/event.ts. No migration ships with this diff (zero apps/bot/drizzle/ files in the diff), so the S13 migration-signoff trigger does not apply.
evidence.s9_extension_check: notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants reuses the existing sendLedgeredNotification unchanged (confirmed via empty diff on domain/notification.ts) in a plain sequential loop, one call per candidate -- not a new, parallel send mechanism. The ledger's unique index on (registrationId, kind) remains the sole idempotency mechanism; notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants keeps no in-memory state. Verified for real with AC2's DB test: 2 sends on run 1, 0 on run 2, exactly 1 ledger row per registration total.
evidence.s10_check: classification: 'transactional' is a hardcoded literal at the single sendLedgeredNotification call site inside notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants, unconditional, no branch or config path could vary it. sendLedgeredNotification's broadcastOptIn check is gated strictly on classification === 'marketing', so a transactional call never reads it. Verified for real with AC3's DB test.
evidence.authorization_check: requireOrganizerForChapter (domain/eventAuthorization.ts, byte-for-byte untouched) still runs before both cancelEvent and the new notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants call, in the same position as before this requirement; the sender parameter only threads a process-wide singleton through and adds no new branch around the existing check.
evidence.repeated_trigger_finding: Cancel/re-cancel spam is not reachable through the command surface: the event status machine has no reverse transition out of 'cancelled' (grepped every status-set call in domain/event.ts), so the handler's own pre-existing `event.status !== 'published'` guard refuses any second /event_cancel call against the same event BEFORE reaching cancelEvent or notifyNonWithdrawnRegistrants at all. Even setting that guard aside, S9's per-(registrationId,kind) ledger dedup (verified via AC2) would make a hypothetical repeated direct call a no-op regardless -- defense in depth, but the state-machine guard is the actual, sufficient blocker.
evidence.pii_exposure_check: composeCancellationMessage's composed text contains only a static header line, the cancelled event's own title, and an already-existing static onward-path string -- no registrant count, list, or other-registrant data appears anywhere in the message or in any of the three new functions' parameters/return values.
